spec_gap.primary_gap: The packet's deliverable 3 (rational surface arm) plus acceptance tests 5 (`positive_cylinder_admitted`) and 9 (`end_to_end_cylinder_union`) require the certified boolean funnel to consume rational (X,Y,Z,W) patches for a canonical CYLINDER operand and to run MONO-8 admission -> flux -> MONO-5 membership -> MONO-9 fold end to end. The landed funnel is unit-weight and box-only: it has no rational patch representation, no rational patch extraction, and no rational membership. None of those three is among the packet's five deliverables, and the packet's own integration map declares extraction unchanged. The admission widening therefore exposes the CYLINDER x CYLINDER pair class to a contact-cover layer whose hypotheses (unit-weight `Patch`, box-only `placed_box_patches`) it does not cover.
evidence: bd_bridge.rs:7751 `struct Patch` carries only `rows`, `cols`, `data: Vec<[f64;3]>` and `orientation`; there is no weight channel.

bd_bridge.rs:7758 `parse_patch` returns `MembershipRefusal::RationalWeights` for any `w != 1.0` (bd_bridge.rs:7781-7783). Every MONO-5 membership and flux routine consumes `&Patch`: `patch_range` (7805), `patch_derivative_u` (7832), `patch_derivative_v` (7867), `normal_interval` (7902), `classify_ray` (8327), `cell_flux_exact` (8751). Deliverable 3's 'no dehomogenization, no approximation anywhere in the new path' therefore requires a rational `Patch` and rational membership that the five deliverables do not include.

bd_bridge.rs:4734 `placed_box_patches` matches only `SolidSpec::Box` and returns `BooleanVolumeRefusal::BooleanProductVolumeUnavailable` for every other carrier, including `SolidSpec::Cylinder` (bd_bridge.rs:4743); bd_bridge.rs:4807 `node_box_patches` inherits this for `TreeNode::Part`. `boolean_product_volume_certified` (bd_bridge.rs:4831) calls `node_box_patches` first, so a canonical cylinder operand refuses before any flux runs.

No rational `VolumeRow` is ever produced anywhere in the repository: every `VolumeRow` constructor writes `weights: 1.0` (bd_bridge.rs:2405, 4723, 5367). The only weight-carrying path is the separate RDEF-M2 sandwich probe (`SandwichPatchRow` -> `certify_sandwich_probe`, bd_bridge.rs:10749), which computes a tangential sandwich *bound*, not the certified flux integral `cell_flux_certified` this packet requires.

docs/CERTIFIED_FLUX_CALCULUS_INTEGRATION_MAP.md:18 records 'Patch extraction (`node_box_patches` x3, `placed_box_patches` x2) ... the router's input; unchanged', yet acceptance tests 5 and 9 require exactly the extraction it declares unchanged. The normative theory is absent: no file in the repository contains the owner's Certified Flux Calculus proposal. docs/CERTIFIED_FLUX_CALCULUS_INTEGRATION_MAP.md and PACKET.md reference its sections 5 (Theorem 5.2 reciprocal-power kernel), 6/6.1 (exponent-3 reduction, sign admission), 8 and 13, but the packet states neither the bivariate certified tail `R_{k,r}(delta)` nor the section-6.1 sign-admission rule nor the section-13 routing order. The only landed reciprocal-power object is the univariate `certified_reciprocal_power` (vendor/truck/truck-evidence/src/num/reciprocal.rs:338), which takes a 1-D Bernstein coefficient slice, returns a 1-D `ReciprocalPower`, and is not consumed by truck123d (grep 'reciprocal' in truck123d/src returns nothing). The predecessor T1-T6 statement (docs/BOOLEAN_MACHINERY_THEORY_GAP.md) is explicitly superseded by the absent proposal, so implementing it would relitigate the theory the packet says not to relitigate.
